data.content_ref: inline:{"analogy":null,"claim":"A finite-field obstruction at p=2 or p=3 explains the stall at 23 multiplications for 3x3 matrix multiplication: the tensor rank of <3,3,3> over F_p is > 22, precluding a rank-22 decomposition over the integers.","counterconditions":[{"case":"The tensor rank of <3,3,3> over F_p is found to be <= 22 for all tested primes, falsifying the finite-field lower bound obstruction.","eval":"observation"},{"case":"A valid rank-22 decomposition over the integers is found and sandbox-verified, invalidating the claim that rank > 22.","eval":"observation"},{"case":"The simulation's flattening rank computation incorrectly evaluates the Strassen 2x2 calibration case, proving the simulation method is flawed.","eval":"observation"}],"definitions":[],"derivation":[],"formalization_refs":[],"mechanism":"We propose a sandboxed Python simulation (simulation_mode sandboxed_python_v1) that reduces the 729 tensor entry equations of <3,3,3> modulo small primes (p=2, 3). The program first calibrates by verifying Strassen's 2x2 rank-7 over F_p and rejecting a corrupted copy. It then computes the tensor rank over F_p using linear algebra (flattening matrices and checking matrix rank). If the tensor rank over F_p is > 22 for any prime p, then no integer rank-22 decomposition can exist because any such integer decomposition would yield a valid decomposition modulo p. This provides a decidable, computable structural obstruction explaining the lack of progress below 23.","premises":[],"schema":"deepreason-reasoning-envelope-v1","scope":{"covers":[],"excludes":[]},"simulation_refs":[],"uncertainties":[]}
